answer: Each of 379 aliases needs its own serial registries, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. A luthier workshop record with instrument serial registry works as the gate: instruments built and registered under one maker for years. The jade check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. The plume record is public, the juniper cost is per identity, and 379 aliases cost 379 times one honest seat.
